fit.gap_handling_summary: The CV honestly presents a junior, frontend-led candidate rather than manufacturing two years of professional full-stack experience. It preserves the internship, part-time freelance status, academic project context and WCAG 2.1 level. Accessibility, unit testing, Storybook and the booking website are relevant strengths, but backend delivery, end-to-end testing, security and health-data privacy remain unproven. The letter connects the strengths to the role but offers little explicit discussion of the learning gaps.

artefacts: PDF extraction joins the institution and dates: 'Liffey Institute of Technology2021–2025'.
PDF extraction loses spacing in 'Computing –Software Development' and '“Tidewatch,”an accessible'.
issues: The education title, institution, dates and honours are crowded together in the PDF; the honours wrap awkwardly.
The summary is accurate but largely a skills inventory rather than a sharply differentiated patient-experience profile.
Backend capabilities are listed without evidence of service or database implementation beyond the academic project's Node.js stack.

reasons: Clear standard headings, one-column structure and largely sensible extraction support parsing.
The principal React/TypeScript stack and several relevant tools are present.
The dated experience does not establish the required two years of professional React/TypeScript development.
End-to-end testing, security and privacy keywords are absent, and professional backend implementation is not demonstrated.
Minor extraction joins affect the education entry but do not make the CV generally unreadable.

issues: The delivered cover-letter document begins with a complete duplicate CV, not a standalone letter.
This duplication expands the PDF to two pages and buries the actual application letter.
The 'COVER LETTER' heading and salutation are left at the bottom of page one, while all substantive letter paragraphs start on page two.
The actual prose is credible but largely restates CV evidence; it does not explicitly address the step up to professional full-stack work or the missing end-to-end testing and security experience.
strengths: Names Verdane Care, the Full-Stack Engineer role and the Patient Experience team.
Uses the company's actual 'Patients first,' 'Privacy by default' and 'Simple beats clever' principles.
Makes a sensible connection between accessibility fixes, a booking website and patient-facing software.
Keeps academic work clearly identified as a final-year project and avoids invented experience.
The letter body alone has a professional tone and an appropriate length.

overflow_or_cutoff: In the CV education entry, the institution name runs directly into the right-aligned dates ('Technology2021–2025'), leaving no clear separation.
spacing_issues: The CV's education metadata is cramped, with 'Honours' wrapped onto its own line.
The cover-letter heading and salutation are stranded at the foot of page one.
The cover-letter PDF's second page is only 41.1% filled because the duplicated CV consumes the first page.
consistency_issues: The CV has a centred header, dark headings and blue rules; the cover-letter document has a left-aligned header, blue headings and dark rules.
The duplicated CV inside the cover-letter file uses different date placement and a larger body size than the actual CV.
issues: The CV is otherwise a readable, compact one-page document with clear sections and visible links.
The cover-letter PDF is professionally legible at 11 pt but structurally unsuitable as a standalone letter.
The CV's 10 pt body is usable, though the education entry needs more space.

The job also permits fully remote work within Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia; the single arrangement category cannot capture both this option and Graz hybrid work. Neither output invents a commitment or rules the candidate out.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'These experiences align with the role’s emphasis' is generic application phrasing, although the preceding evidence is relevant.
'technical foundation could contribute' is cautious but vague about the specific contribution the candidate could make.

evaluation.summary: The CV is factually faithful and retains all relevant supplied evidence, particularly accessibility fixes, Storybook, unit testing and booking-site development. It honestly presents a junior frontend candidate whose experience does not yet establish the advertised professional full-stack requirements. The letter's prose is appropriately targeted to Verdane Care, but the delivered document incorrectly includes the entire CV before the letter, producing an avoidable two-page file with a stranded salutation. The CV also needs a small education-layout repair; neither document invents experience or work-arrangement commitments.
